title: The join slice and fixed-target arrow category are equivalent
statement:
Use quasicategories, internal functor simplicial sets and equivalences of quasicategories as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal C$ be a small quasicategory in the fixed universe and $y$ a vertex. Define the simplicial set $S_y$ by
$$ (S_y)_n=\{\sigma:\Delta^{n+1}\to\mathcal C\mid\sigma(n+1)=y\}.$$
For $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, its operator is precomposition with $\alpha^+:[m+1]\to[n+1]$, where $\alpha^+(a)=\alpha(a)$ for $a\leq m$ and $\alpha^+(m+1)=n+1$. Write $p_y:S_y\to\mathcal C$ for restriction to the initial face $\Delta^n$. Define
$$T_y=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,\mathcal C}\{y\},\qquad q_y=\operatorname{ev}_0:T_y\to\mathcal C.$$
For each $n$, let $\rho_n:\Delta^n\times\Delta^1\to\Delta^{n+1}$ be the nerve of the monotone map $[n]\times[1]\to[n+1]$ given by $(a,0)\mapsto a$ and $(a,1)\mapsto n+1$. Define $\delta_y:S_y\to T_y$ in degree $n$ by $\sigma\mapsto\sigma\circ\rho_n$, with the factors interchanged for the internal-functor convention. Then $S_y$ and $T_y$ are quasicategories, and $\delta_y$ is an equivalence of quasicategories over $\mathcal C$: it is an equivalence and $q_y\delta_y=p_y$.

source.place: Corollary 4.6.4.20, slice assertion; Construction 4.6.4.15 (02GH) specifies the slice diagonal. Read online 2026-10-16, not archived under literature/. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags.

proof.text: First check the actual map and its equation over the base, using the degreewise constructions of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. For every $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, one has $\rho_n(\alpha\times\mathrm{id})=\alpha^+\rho_m$: both maps take $(a,0)$ to $\alpha(a)$ and $(a,1)$ to $n+1$. Thus $\sigma\mapsto\sigma\rho_n$ commutes with every simplicial operator. Its restriction to the top layer is the constant simplex at $y$, so it lies in $T_y$; its restriction to the bottom layer is the entire initial face of $\sigma$. Consequently $q_y\delta_y=p_y$ as simplicial maps, including all degeneracies. Factor interchange changes only the order of coordinates in the internal-hom convention.

source.place: Construction 4.6.4.15; explicit formula for the point-indexed slice diagonal.

proof.text: The join slice $S_y$ is a quasicategory directly from the inner-horn axiom in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. More precisely $p_y$ is a right fibration: a right-horn lifting problem with $\Lambda_i^m\hookrightarrow\Delta^m$, $0<i\leq m$, specifies the initial $m$-face in $\mathcal C$ from the base simplex and all coned faces except the $i$th from the slice horn. Their intersections agree, so together they are $\Lambda_i^{m+1}\to\mathcal C$. This horn is inner since $0<i<m+1$, and its filler gives the slice lift. For an inner horn in $S_y$, first fill its projection in $\mathcal C$ and then use this right-fibration lifting property. For $T_y$, [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration] applies to precisely the given arrow pullback and says $q_y$ is a right fibration. Fill the projection of any inner horn in $T_y$ in $\mathcal C$ and lift that filler along $q_y$. Thus both total spaces are quasicategories; no assumptions on their fibers are needed.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.4.13 for the fixed-target arrow projection; the right-slice horn calculation expands Kerodon Proposition 4.3.6.1 (018F).

proof.text: For any small simplicial set $J$, form its right cone $J^{\triangleright}$ by concatenating simplices of $J$ with constant simplices at a new last vertex $*$. Let $\mathcal A_J=\operatorname{Fun}(J^{\triangleright},\mathcal C)\times_{\mathcal C}\{y\}$, with projection evaluation at $*$. Maps $e:J\to S_y$ are in bijection with vertices $F_e$ of $\mathcal A_J$: for every $a:\Delta^n\to J$ set $F_ea^{\triangleright}=e_n(a)$; compatibility of these simplices is exactly $e\alpha=\alpha^+e$, and they cover the cone. Conversely restrict a cone map to these coned simplices. Also define the blunt right cone $B_J=(J\times\Delta^1)\amalg_{J\times\{1\}}\{*\}$. A vertex of $\operatorname{Fun}(J,T_y)$ is exactly a map $B_J\to\mathcal C$ sending $*$ to $y$: transpose the internal functor by the product rule in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. In every parameter degree $r$ the same rule identifies $\operatorname{Fun}(J,T_y)$ with the strict fiber at $y$ of $\operatorname{Fun}(B_J,\mathcal C)$. The comparison $c_J:B_J\to J^{\triangleright}$ sends $(a,t)$ to the concatenation of the initial $0$-block of $t$ with the last-vertex $1$-block. On the cone on $a:\Delta^n\to J$ this is exactly $\rho_n$. Hence precomposition by $c_J$ sends $F_e$ to the vertex $\delta_y e$.

source.place: Construction 4.6.4.15 and Remark 4.6.4.16; explicit specialization of blunt and ordinary joins to a point. This is a degreewise universal-property calculation, not an assertion that the two diagram simplicial sets in the first bijection are isomorphic.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-coef-infinity-blunt-sharp-join-equivalence] with $X=J$, $Y=\Delta^0$, and $\mathcal E=\mathcal C$. Its sharp and blunt joins are precisely $J^{\triangleright}$ and $B_J$ from step 3, and its comparison restricts on every coned simplex to $\rho_n$. It gives a functor equivalence
$$u_J:\operatorname{Fun}(J^{\triangleright},\mathcal C)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(B_J,\mathcal C).$$
Both restriction maps to the distinguished vertex $\{*\}$ are isofibrations between quasicategories by [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-exponentiation], applied to the degreewise injective inclusions $\{*\}\hookrightarrow J^{\triangleright}$ and $\{*\}\hookrightarrow B_J$. Identify $\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^0,\mathcal C)$ with $\mathcal C$ by evaluation. Since $c_J$ is the identity on $\{*\}$, these restrictions satisfy $\operatorname{ev}_*u_J=\operatorname{ev}_*$ strictly. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-isofibration-base-change] with these two restriction maps, base $\mathcal S=\mathcal C$, test quasicategory $\mathcal R=\Delta^0$, and $h(*)=y$. Its conclusion gives an equivalence of the ordinary simplicial fibers
$$r_J:\mathcal A_J\longrightarrow\operatorname{Fun}(B_J,\mathcal C)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_*,\mathcal C}\{y\}\cong\operatorname{Fun}(J,T_y).$$
The last isomorphism is the degreewise calculation in step 3. Thus $r_J$ sends $F_e$ to $\delta_y e$, and the cone vertex is constant throughout each parameter simplex. This uses base change along two isofibrations, not preservation of arbitrary strict fibers by an equivalence.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.6.4.19, final diagram: Theorem 4.6.2.8 (01HV), restriction isofibrations (01F3), and invariance of isofibration pullbacks (03PM). Point-indexed specialization with all fiber maps identified.

proof.text: By [lem-cbc-internal-hom-quasicategory] and step 2, $\operatorname{Fun}(J,S_y)$ and $\operatorname{Fun}(J,T_y)$ are quasicategories for every small $J$. The fiber category $\mathcal A_J$ is a quasicategory by step 4's base-change theorem. Pass to equivalence classes of vertices, where two vertices represent the same class when there is a coherent natural equivalence between them. For $\operatorname{Fun}(J,S_y)$ and $\mathcal A_J$, [lem-coef-join-slice-diagram-isomorphisms] says exactly that the object bijection $e\mapsto F_e$ from step 3 preserves and reflects this relation. Hence it induces a bijection of classes. The functor $r_J$ of step 4 also induces a bijection of classes: a quasi-inverse gives surjectivity and, applied to an equivalence between two images and followed by the inverse's natural equivalence with the identity, gives injectivity. By $r_J(F_e)=\delta_y e$, their composite is precisely the map induced by postcomposition with $\delta_y$. Therefore this postcomposition is bijective on equivalence classes of $J$-diagrams for every small $J$. All equivalences of cone diagrams fix the vertex throughout. The equivalence convention is that of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.6.4.19, the displayed map on components of functor cores, with Lemma 4.6.4.25 (01KV) specialized to a point; expanded as classes of naturally equivalent objects.

proof.text: Use that bijectivity only for $J=T_y$ and $J=S_y$, both small quasicategories by step 2. Surjectivity for $J=T_y$ produces $g:T_y\to S_y$ and a coherent natural equivalence $\delta_yg\simeq\mathrm{id}_{T_y}$. Whisker this equivalence on the right by $\delta_y$. This gives a coherent natural equivalence between $\delta_y(g\delta_y)$ and $\delta_y=\delta_y\mathrm{id}_{S_y}$; the inverse and its two triangle witnesses are whiskered by the same substitution. Injectivity for $J=S_y$ now gives $g\delta_y\simeq\mathrm{id}_{S_y}$. These are exactly the quasi-inverse and the two coherent natural equivalences in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], so $\delta_y$ is an equivalence. Its strict equation over $\mathcal C$ was already verified in step 1. The assertion requires no chosen quasi-inverse over $\mathcal C$.

source.place: Proof of Theorem 4.6.4.19; agent expansion of equivalence recognition from bijectivity on diagram isomorphism classes.
